alt_text: Photo in Passeig de Gràcia, Barcelona. Text on the image: Used to work or used to working?
caption:
"I'm used to working late" and "I used to work late" look almost identical, but they say opposite things about your present. I'm used to working late: it's normal for me now. I'm familiar with it. Here, "to" is a preposition, so it's followed by -ing. I used to work late: I did it in the past, but I don't anymore. Here, "used to" is followed by the base verb. A common slip is "I'm used to work late." If there is a form of "be" before "used to", the verb that follows needs -ing. A quick test: can you swap in "familiar with"? If so, use -ing. If you mean "I did this regularly before", use used to + verb. Try it with your own schedule: what are you used to, and what did you use to do?
